rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to spread unknown compounds across the run while likely eluting all 10 within the 42 min window. This first run should reveal overall retention range, crowding, and whether stronger or shallower conditions are needed next.

All 10 compounds eluted with baseline resolution and the chromatogram finished very early, so the main opportunity is to reduce the time penalty. Lowering phi1 while keeping the same gradient length and temperature should retain late compounds a bit longer without risking loss, while compressing the gradient strength to improve overall time-efficiency and test whether selectivity around peaks 5–7 changes favorably.

The first run already had perfect resolution and a modest time penalty, so the best direction is to shorten the gradient substantially while keeping the successful composition range. This should pull the last peak earlier and improve CRF unless the critical mid-cluster around peaks 5–7 begins to compress too much.

The 12 min gradient is very fast but slightly under-resolves the critical pair, so a small increase in gradient time should restore resolution with little or no time penalty term. This is a local optimization around the current best conditions.

The current method is very close to ideal, with only the 6/7 pair slightly below 1.5, so a small additional increase in gradient time is the most direct way to push that pair over the threshold while likely keeping the time term at zero. This probes whether the optimum is just beyond 14 min.

Since 14 min is near-optimal in time but the critical pair is just short of full baseline resolution, the next lever to test is selectivity via temperature rather than making the run longer. A modest drop to 35 C may improve the 6/7 separation enough to reach CRF 1.0 while keeping all peaks within the zero time-penalty region.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity, so test the opposite direction while keeping the near-optimal 14 min gradient fixed. A modest increase to 45 C may improve the critical mid-cluster separation enough to push the current best method to full score without incurring a time penalty.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so keep the successful 14 min, 40 C conditions and adjust only the starting strength to reshape the crowded early-mid region. Lowering phi0 should spread the first part of the chromatogram and may improve the critical 6/7 separation while likely keeping the run within the no-penalty time range.

Changing phi0 downward gave a small selectivity shift but did not beat the original, so test the symmetric adjustment upward to see whether the critical pair benefits in the opposite direction. This keeps the run in the proven high-CRF region while probing a remaining simple selectivity lever.

The optimum is very narrow around the original settings, so the next clean test is a slight reduction in gradient end strength to alter late-gradient slope and local selectivity near the critical pair. This should preserve full elution and may nudge the 6/7 resolution above 1.5 without adding a time penalty.

A small step down in phi1 from the optimum tests whether the full-score plateau extends to slightly weaker final strength, which could improve robustness around the critical pair while likely staying in the zero time-penalty region. This is a conservative neighbor search around the proven optimum.

Now that phi1 = 0.85 is confirmed optimal at phi0 = 0.10, test whether a slightly lower starting strength broadens the early-mid cluster while retaining the full-score behavior. This is a close local probe around the optimum with minimal risk of losing compounds or incurring time penalty.

The full-score region appears centered near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so test the diagonal neighbor at slightly higher phi0 and lower phi1 to map the robustness boundary. This stays near the optimum while checking whether maximum CRF extends along a correlated change in gradient window.

Most of the immediate neighborhood around the optimum has been mapped, so test one remaining nearby corner combining higher phi0 with lower phi1. This helps define the boundary of the full-score region and whether resolution of the critical pair can be preserved under a narrower gradient window.

A second full-score point was found by moving along the phi0-up/phi1-down direction, so continue one more step to locate the edge of that maximum-score ridge. This is the most informative nearby unexplored point for defining the robust optimum region.

The edge was crossed at phi0 = 0.25, phi1 = 0.80, so the next best local probe is to lower phi1 one step while staying at the successful phi0 = 0.20. This tests whether the full-score ridge continues toward a still narrower gradient window without the severe early coelution seen at higher phi0.

Since phi0 = 0.25 caused early coelution at phi1 = 0.80, test whether restoring a slightly stronger gradient end rescues that early pair while keeping the successful 14 min format. This clarifies whether the failure at phi0 = 0.25 was due to too narrow a gradient window rather than phi0 alone.

At phi0 = 0.20, both lower phi1 values have been explored, but the stronger-end counterpart has not. Testing phi1 = 0.90 completes the local map around this high-performing ridge and shows whether the full-score plateau also extends upward in final strength at phi0 = 0.20.

For the final shot, test the remaining low-phi0/low-phi1 corner near the successful 14 min, 40 C region to complete the local composition map opposite the high-phi0 ridge. It is unlikely to beat the existing 1.000, but it is the most informative nearby unexplored condition.
